lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. It is seven a.m. on a Saturday, and she planned to sleep until lunch.
**Kavya:** Why is the sun in my face? It's Saturday. The sun doesn't even go to school.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is not about Kavya. It is about the thing that just hit her in the face.
**Narrator:** This is him.
**Ray:** Hi. Ray. I'm a **ray of light**. I work in deliveries.
**Ray:** I left the Sun eight minutes ago. A hundred and fifty million kilometres. In a **straight line**.
**Narrator:** Light travels at about **300,000 km/s**. Nothing is faster.
**Ray:** And always in **straight lines**. I don't do curves. I don't do shortcuts. I don't do scenic routes.
**Ray:** My boss is the Sun. **Luminous**: makes its own light. Never lets anyone forget it.
**Ray:** All that, to wake up one twelve-year-old.
**Ray:** Nobody tips.
**Narrator:** Light Work. Episode ten: Return to Sender.
**Narrator:** Seven oh five. Ray comes through the window. Glass is **transparent**: light goes straight through.
**Ray:** The curtains are **translucent**. They let me in, but scatter me everywhere. Unprofessional.
**Narrator:** Kavya pulls the blanket over her head. The blanket is **opaque**. No light gets through at all.
**Ray:** Opaque. Fine. I'll leave it with the neighbour.
**Ray:** Here's the job. Light bounces off things and goes **into your eye**. That's how you **see** them.
**Kavya:** Wait. I thought my eyes sent something out. Like little lasers.
**Ray:** No.
**Ray:** Your eyes don't send anything out. They only **receive** light. You're not a superhero. You're a letterbox.
**Narrator:** Her wall makes no light of its own. It's **non-luminous**.
**Kavya:** But the Moon glows. So the Moon makes light, right?
**Ray:** The Moon is **non-luminous**. It just reflects our sunlight, and takes all the credit.
**Narrator:** Fully awake and fully annoyed, Kavya makes a shadow puppet with her phone torch.
**Kavya:** It's a dinosaur. Roar.
**Ray:** Light travels in straight lines, so her hand **blocks** me. The dark patch behind it is a **shadow**.
**Narrator:** She moves her hand **closer to the torch**. The shadow gets **bigger**.
**Kavya:** Big dinosaur. Roar.
**Narrator:** A big lamp gives a fuzzy shadow: a dark **umbra**, and a lighter **penumbra**.
**Narrator:** Seven fifteen. The bathroom. Next stop for Ray: a very important client.
**Mirabel:** Hello, darling. Mirabel. **Plane mirror**. Flat, shiny, and frankly stunning.
**Ray:** Mirabel reflects everything. Mostly, she reflects on herself.
**Norman:** Excuse me. Norman. **The normal**. An imaginary line at **90°** to the surface.
**Ray:** Norman turns up whenever light hits a surface. He's imaginary. He comes anyway.
**Norman:** All angles are measured from me. **Not** from the mirror. From **me**.
**Mirabel:** The angle coming in equals the angle going out, darling. I'm a professional.
**Narrator:** That's **the law of reflection**: the **angle of incidence** equals the **angle of reflection**. **i = r**.
**Narrator:** The towel is rough, so it scatters light in all directions. That's **diffuse reflection**.
**Mirabel:** Whereas I'm smooth: **regular reflection**. Parallel rays stay parallel, so you see a clear picture. In me.
**Narrator:** Kavya's image seems to be **behind** the mirror, as far behind as she is in front.
**Norman:** But no light actually goes behind the mirror. The image is **virtual**. You can't catch it on a screen.
**Mirabel:** Virtual? My reflection is the most real thing in this flat!
**Norman:** It's virtual, Mirabel.
**Narrator:** A plane mirror image is **virtual**, **upright**, the **same size**, and **laterally inverted**. **V U S L**.
**Kavya:** I'm waving my right hand. My reflection is waving her left.
**Mirabel:** But I never turn you upside down, darling. I'm a mirror, not a roller coaster.
**Narrator:** Two p.m. The swimming complex. **33 °C**. Ray dives in.
**Dennis:** Hello. I'm Dennis. I'm the water. People say I'm dense.
**Dennis:** I prefer... **optically dense**.
**Narrator:** Light travels **more slowly** in water than in air. Entering a new **medium** at an angle, that change in speed makes Ray **bend**: **refraction**.
**Kavya:** So light bends because it's taking a shortcut?
**Ray:** I don't do shortcuts. It's the **change in speed** that bends me.
**Norman:** Into a denser medium, he slows down and bends **towards** the normal. Towards me.
**Norman:** Out into a less dense one, he speeds up and bends **away** from me.
**Norman:** People think light always bends towards me. I wish. Only when it slows down.
**Narrator:** Remember: **SloTo, FastAway**.
**Ray:** If I go in **along** the normal, I still slow down. But I don't bend at all.
**Narrator:** Light bends as it leaves the water, so the pool looks **shallower** than it really is.
**Dennis:** I'm deeper than I look. People say that about me a lot.
**Kavya:** So that's why my legs look short in the pool. I thought it was just my legs.
**Narrator:** A **rectangular glass block** bends light twice, in and out. The ray comes out **parallel**, just shifted sideways: **lateral displacement**.
**Narrator:** Inside glass, beyond the **critical angle**, about **42°**, no light escapes. It all reflects back inside.
**Ray:** **Total internal reflection**. It's how we zig-zag down **optical fibres**, carrying your internet.
**Ray:** So when your video buffers, it's not me. I am literally light. It's your Wi-Fi.

chapters.title: Seven colours in a trench coat

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Four p.m. A thunderstorm. Very Singapore.
**Ray:** See the lightning? We always get there first. The thunder's still on its way.
**Narrator:** Light is about a **million times faster** than sound.
**Narrator:** After the rain, sunlight hits a glass **prism** in Grandma's window.
**Ray:** Okay. Time you knew. I'm not one colour.
**Ray:** **White light** is a **mixture** of colours. I'm basically seven colours in a trench coat.
**Narrator:** The prism refracts each colour by a slightly different amount, so the colours **spread out**.
**Violet:** Wheee! Hi! Violet! I bend the **most**!
**Narrator:** Red bends the **least**. Red is very relaxed about everything.
**Narrator:** Out comes the **visible spectrum**: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet. This is **dispersion**.
**Narrator:** To remember the order: **Richard Of York Gave Battle In Vain**.
**Indigo:** Hi. Indigo. Between blue and violet. Some people can't tell me apart from blue.
**Indigo:** I'm a real colour. I have feelings. Mostly blue ones.
**Kavya:** So the prism **made** the rainbow?
**Ray:** No. The prism doesn't **add** any colour. We were in there all along. It just **separates** us.
**Narrator:** Raindrops act like millions of tiny prisms. That's a **rainbow**. You only see one with the Sun **behind** you.
**Narrator:** Six p.m. Drama club rehearsal, in the school hall.
**Kavya:** I'm Tree Number Three. I have no lines. This is fine.
**Narrator:** White light hits a red prop apple. It **reflects** red light and **absorbs** all the other colours.
**Ray:** Only red reaches your eye. The apple doesn't glow, and it doesn't turn the light red.
**Narrator:** A **white** object reflects **all** the colours. A **black** object absorbs them all.
**Rosie:** Name's Rosie. **Red filter**. I work the spotlight. Let me check the list.
**Rosie:** Red? You're on the list. Green? Blue? Not on the list.
**Narrator:** A **filter** **transmits** its own colour and **absorbs** the others. Remember: **a filter is selfish**.
**Rosie:** Selfish? I prefer exclusive.
**Narrator:** Under Rosie's red light, Kavya's green leaves have no green light to reflect.
**Kavya:** Why are my leaves black? I'm a tree. Trees are green.
**Rosie:** Green? Not on the list.
**Narrator:** Next: red, green and blue spotlights, the **primary colours of light**.
**Narrator:** **Red + green = yellow. Green + blue = cyan. Red + blue = magenta.** All three make **white**.
**Ray:** All three together? That's white. That's me. Hi again.
**Narrator:** Phone screens use tiny **red, green and blue** dots. No yellow dots at all.
**Narrator:** **Paints** are different: they **absorb** light, so mixing them makes darker, muddier colours.
**Narrator:** Ten p.m. Kavya is reading in bed. Ray makes his last delivery: straight into her eye.
**Ray:** First, the **cornea**, the clear window at the front. It does **most** of the bending.
**Ray:** Then the **pupil**. It's not really a part. It's a hole. I go through the hole.
**Narrator:** The **iris**, a coloured ring of muscle, makes the pupil **smaller** in bright light, **wider** in dim light.
**Ray:** Next, the **lens**. It fine-tunes the focus. It's squishy. Like Dennis, if Dennis did yoga.
**Narrator:** To focus on her book, the **ciliary muscles** contract. The lens gets **fatter**, and bends light **more**.
**Narrator:** For the clock across the room, they relax. The **suspensory ligaments** pull the lens **thinner**. This is **accommodation**.
**Ray:** Last stop, the **retina**, at the back. The picture lands here. Upside down.
**Kavya:** Upside down? I've been seeing upside down my whole life?
**Narrator:** The image is **real** and **inverted**. The **optic nerve** carries signals to the **brain**, which sees it the right way up.
**Ray:** Twelve years of upside-down pictures. Her brain quietly fixes every one. Nobody tips the brain either.
**Narrator:** Ten fifteen. Kavya switches off the light.
**Ray:** Shift over. See you at seven.

chapters.title: The cast saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the credits, the cast would like to save you some marks.
**Norman:** One. Measure every angle from the **normal**. Never from the surface. Never.
**Mirabel:** Two. A plane mirror image is **virtual**, not real. It hurts me to say it.
**Dennis:** Three. Light bends towards the normal **only** when it slows down, going into a **denser** medium.
**Violet:** Four! **Violet** bends the most! **Red** bends the least! Not the other way round!
**Ray:** Five. A prism doesn't **add** colour. It only **separates** the colours already there.
**Rosie:** Six. A red apple doesn't turn light red. It **reflects** red and **absorbs** the rest.
**Kavya:** Seven. Your eyes don't send anything out. They only **receive** light.
**Narrator:** Light Work will return.
**Indigo:** Did anyone notice I was here?
**Ray:** Course we did, Blue.
**Indigo:** ...Indigo.
